read: partial: pp.1-9 (abstract, introduction, symbolic templates, evaluation setup, difficulty metrics, beam search, results, fine-tuning) read in full; Appendix B.3 (EngTrace, p.16) and D.2.2 (FinChain and EngTrace results, pp.24-25) read; the other appendices, figures and prompts (pp.10-41) skimmed.
venue_now: arXiv 2605.15393v1 [cs.LG], 14 May 2026 (page 1 stamp; dated 18 May 2026); FAIR at Meta and LMU Munich; no venue
what_it_is: LPDS is a method, not a benchmark: it estimates how hard a logic-preserving variation of a symbolic template is for a given model, by the distance of the model's response from its own correct responses to other variations of the template (normalised Levenshtein LDmin; hidden-state Mahalanobis MDH), and searches the template's variable space by beam search for the variations that maximise that difficulty (pp.4-6). It uses 100 templates each from GSM-Symbolic, FinChain and EngTrace, the last taken from EngTrace's public repository of the 90-template release, with structure-changing templates split and value ranges narrowed (pp.3, 16). On seven open models (Llama 3.x, Qwen 2.5, Phi-4), beam search finds variations whose accuracy drop is up to five times that of random sampling (pp.1, 7-8), and error rates, and the rate at which accuracy falls with difficulty, are highest on the EngTrace templates (pp.24-25). Fine-tuning on harder variations gives more consistent robustness gains (GSM-Symbolic, FinChain; p.9).
domain: grade-school math (GSM-Symbolic), finance (FinChain) and engineering (EngTrace's chemical, electrical and mechanical templates)
size: 100 templates per dataset; 1,000 variations per template (100,000 per dataset) for the metric analysis (p.5); seven models (p.3)
source_of_items: existing symbolic templates from GSM-Symbolic, FinChain and EngTrace's public repository, adapted by the authors (pp.3, 16)
instances: generated (variations searched by beam search within each template's variable space)
has_gold_traces: n/a (method): the templates' ground-truth reasoning traces serve as fine-tuning targets (p.9), but the difficulty metrics use the model's own correct responses as the reference, not the gold trace (p.4)
evaluation: final answer: five-shot chain-of-thought, greedy decoding, last number parsed; exact match for GSM-Symbolic and a tolerance of 1e-6 + 1% of the answer for FinChain and EngTrace (p.4); the difficulty metrics are assessed by AUC and odds ratios for predicting correctness (p.5)
human_validation: none reported (no new items; the authors adapted existing templates)
contamination_measures: the paper's premise is that symbolic variations expose contamination and reliance on surface patterns (pp.2-3); it adds an adversarial search over variations rather than a new dataset

engtrace_use.explanation: Not cited in the May paper. Paragraph: math and coding (symbolic-template robustness, beside GSM-Symbolic), or the introduction's sentence on symbolic templates; it also bears on the Limitations. A reviewer would expect it for three reasons: it is third-party use of EngTrace's templates; it reports that variations from EngTrace's templates are the hardest of its three sets and that accuracy falls fastest on them as difficulty rises (pp.24-25); and it names EngTrace among benchmarks whose randomly sampled instances 'can overestimate robustness' (p.2). The revision must answer that critique: EngTrace's 15 instances per template are chosen round-robin over reasoning paths and answer forms from the first 100 draws, not searched for difficulty, so its scores describe typical rather than worst-case instances. It must also say that LPDS used the earlier public 90-template release, as modified by its authors (p.16), not the present private pool.

suggested_wording: LPDS (Mondorf et al., 2026) shows that scoring a random sample of a template's variations, as GSM-Symbolic, FinChain and the earlier release of EngTrace do, overstates robustness: a beam search over logic-preserving variations finds much harder instances, and accuracy falls fastest on the engineering templates.
facts_to_cite: LPDS scores the difficulty of a logic-preserving variation by the distance of the model's response from its correct responses to other variations of the same template (normalised Levenshtein LDmin; hidden-state Mahalanobis MDH) (p.4).
For Llama-3.1-8B, MDH predicts answer correctness with AUC from 0.74 (FinChain) to 0.80 (GSM-Symbolic) and an odds ratio of 0.02 on EngTrace (p.5).

A beam search over variable substitutions finds harder variations; on GSM-Symbolic the accuracy drop relative to GSM8K is up to five times that of random sampling, e.g. 17.6 against 9.7 points for Llama-3.2-3B and 9.0 against 2.2 for Qwen-2.5-72B (pp.1, 7-8).

It uses 100 templates each from GSM-Symbolic, FinChain and EngTrace (p.3); the EngTrace templates come from the public repository of the 90-template release, with templates whose variables change the solution structure split into separate templates and value ranges restricted (p.16).

Seven open models (Llama-3.2-3B, Llama-3.1-8B and 70B, Qwen-2.5-7B, 32B and 72B, Phi-4), five-shot chain-of-thought, greedy decoding, final numeric answer within 1e-6 + 1% for FinChain and EngTrace (pp.3-4).

Error rates are higher on FinChain and EngTrace than on GSM-Symbolic, up to 74.3% for Llama-3.2-3B on beam-searched EngTrace variations (p.24); accuracy drops 'fastest and most substantially' on EngTrace variations as difficulty rises (p.25).
Fine-tuning on harder variations gives more consistent robustness gains than fine-tuning on easier ones (GSM-Symbolic, p.9; FinChain in the appendix).
It cites EngTrace among benchmarks evaluated on a randomly sampled subset of instances, which 'can overestimate robustness' (p.2).
overlap_with_engtrace: Shares: symbolic templates and logic-preserving variation as the robustness probe, applied to EngTrace's own earlier templates (pp.3, 16). Lacks: step-level evaluation (final answer only, p.4); a benchmark of its own; frontier or closed models (seven open models up to 72B, p.3). For EngTrace it implies that random or round-robin instance sampling gives an average-case, not a worst-case, picture of robustness (pp.2, 7-8), and that EngTrace's paraphrase arm tests wording, not adversarially chosen values. It also found that some earlier EngTrace templates switch solution structure on a variable's value (p.16), which the revised pool records as reasoning-path groups rather than splitting the template.
notes: Paragraph: math and coding, or the introduction; also Limitations. (1) LPDS worked from the public 90-template release (github.com/usmansafdarktk/EngTrace, footnote on p.16), split some templates, narrowed ranges and selected 100 (p.16); its numbers do not describe the revised 150-template pool. (2) EngTrace-specific numbers: error rate up to 74.3% for Llama-3.2-3B on beam-searched variations (p.24); accuracy drops fastest on EngTrace (p.25); MDH odds ratio 0.02 on EngTrace (p.5). (3) It cites EngTrace as Gull et al. (2025); the anonymous ARR version should acknowledge it in the third person. (4) The search note is accurate; add that the models are small open models (3B to 72B) under five-shot chain-of-thought, which limits what the result says about current models, and that the fine-tuning experiments do not use EngTrace (p.9).
